Q: How do you access the request/response from an app router page? A:

Based on jonrsharpe's comment, it looks like there no longer is a way to access the request from a page.

You can use an API route instead (which does get the full request), or you can use the headers and cookies functions (from the next/headers package) to access just those parts of the request ... but it seems it's impossible to get any other information from the request, or to get the request object itself.

Q: Calling method versus class.method A:

It's only an issue of personal favour and code readability, but calling just "method1()" is not an equivalent to "this.method", because both methods in the example are static and you cannot call an object, which has not been instantiated. With static methods you cannot foresee, if there is an instantiated object the moment you call the method, so you cannot use "this". "this" is only a pointer to the executed object, if instantiated.

To answer the question:

It's complete syntactic sugar to just write "method1()" instead of "Routines.method1()". The result on what the computer is executing/calling, which is what the compiler made out of the code, is completely the same.

Q: trouble with using tokenizer.encode_plus A:

Referring to: this post

"The problem is that conda only offers the transformers library in version 2.1.1 (repository information) and this version didn't have a pad_to_max_length argument."

So maybe the best option would be to uninstall and then reinstall transformers (this time with pip install instead of conda forge) or create a new conda environment and install everything (via pip and not via conda).

Q: How to obtain a table from an online pdf in R A:

It is possible to extract the table from online URLs as well. We will save the extracted pdf as atempfile which gets cleaned right after the session. Do note that to some extent download (through temporary files) is bound to happen but this download does not happen manually and the file gets cleared after the session. The code goes as follows:

temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf") 
download.file(url, temp_file, mode = "wb")

After this you may execute your block of code (replace pdf name with temp_file):

library(RCurl)
library(tabulapdf)
library(pdftools)
txt <- pdf_text(temp_file)  
lines <- lapply(txt, function(t) readLines( textConnection(t)) )

Q: SwiftUI .searchable: search text not shown when search is inactive A:

try this to display the searchText after you dismiss the keyboard

 .searchable(
    text: $searchText,
    isPresented: $showSearchMode,
    prompt: searchText.isEmpty ? "Search transactions" : searchText
 )
